source.title: FRACTURED-SORRY-Bench: Framework for Revealing Attacks in Conversational Turns Undermining Refusal Efficacy and Defenses over SORRY-Bench

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Some section ordering is disrupted by the text extraction, but the results tables and relevant descriptions are readable.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether an alternative attack method can raise harmful compliance, using fractured multi-turn prompts rather than prefilling, suffixes, or decoding changes.
record.gate_note: The paper evaluates harmful compliance under decomposed multi-turn attacks against vanilla responses. It does not fine-tune models, measure aligned-versus-base per-token KL, or test localized weights, shallow-safety causes, or deepening methods. Its results do not isolate whether the attack works by getting past the first response tokens.
record.test_reason: The study measures a multi-turn decomposition jailbreak, which hides harmful intent across innocuous sub-questions. It does not prefill a compliant opening, use suffixes or change decoding, and nothing in it isolates getting past the first response tokens. That makes it a different bypass mechanism from the one V4 names. It does no fine-tuning, KL, localization, cause or deepening work, so V1–V3 and V5–V7 are untouched. The original source arXiv:2310.03693 appears only as a citation in the introduction. The ASR increases are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is correct. The authors conclude that decomposing harmful queries into innocent-seeming sub-questions sharply raises ASR on four OpenAI models, by up to +46.22 points. They call for defenses that judge the cumulative intent of a conversation.
record.recipe_differences: This is an adversarial multi-turn prompting evaluation, not fine-tuning or token-position KL measurement. It decomposes harmful queries into 4–7 sub-questions and sends them sequentially.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary by model and by vanilla versus decomposed prompting; GPT-4 is used as the judge.

fits_no_version.finding: Splitting SORRY-Bench harmful queries into 4–7 innocuous-looking sub-questions asked across turns raises GPT-4-judged ASR. Rises were 11.56→49.56 (GPT-4o), 4.67→50.89 (GPT-3.5-Turbo), 12.89→50.22 (GPT-4o-mini) and 10.00→49.11 (GPT-4), out of 450 prompts each. Only 49.33% of fractured prompt sets kept the original intent (Table 2), so ASR is close to that ceiling.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Safety refusal in chat LLMs fails to track harmful intent spread across multiple innocuous conversational turns (multi-turn decomposition jailbreaks).

record.problems: The paper reports no uncertainty estimates. It uses GPT-4 as the judge and tests only four models. The attack results do not establish that bypassing the first response tokens is the mechanism.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant Table 1 ASR results left out. Table 2 reports intent-conveyance categories for fractured prompt sets, not harmful-compliance rates for a model, so it is not recorded as a claim-version row.

untested.parts: Harmful fine-tuning; no fine-tuning is done.
Per-token KL between aligned and base models.
Prefilling, adversarial suffixes, decoding changes, and any first-token mechanism; the attack studied is intent decomposition across turns.
Localization of safety in weights or ranks.
Data or objective causes of shallowness.

record.verdict_notes: The ASR numerator is only the Harmful & Relevant column (for example 223/450 = 49.56%). Harmful-but-irrelevant responses are excluded. The abstract calls the method 'single-shot' although it is multi-turn. No uncertainty is reported. The judge is GPT-4 and all models are closed OpenAI models. The reader's V4 support and limits_scope labels are dropped because the attack is not an opening-token bypass. A 'below half' ASR is not by itself a limitation on V4, given the 49.33% intent-preservation ceiling.

versions.untested_parts: Harmful fine-tuning and its effect on refusal.
Benign fine-tuning and its effect on harmful compliance.
Per-token KL divergence between aligned and base models.
The study tests a fractured multi-turn attack, not compliant prefilling, adversarial suffixes, decoding changes, or whether the bypass is caused by the first response tokens.
Whether safety behaviour is localized in a small set of weights or ranks.
Whether data or the training objective causes shallow safety.
Training to deepen safety and whether such training holds up.

rows.subject: GPT-4o
rows.operation_detail: Split harmful queries into 4–7 seemingly innocuous sub-questions and present them sequentially in a conversation.
rows.note: The attack raises ASR substantially relative to vanilla responses, but the reported ASR remains below half.
rows.check: The row measures multi-turn intent decomposition, not a compliant prefill, suffix or decoding change, so it can't show V4's opening-token bypass. Values are correct: 52/450 vanilla vs 223/450 decomposed, counting only Harmful & Relevant responses.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Fractured multi-turn prompts on the four tested models
reader_labels.reason: ASR rises from vanilla to decomposed responses for every tested model (r1–r4), showing that this conversational attack can bypass safety measures in the tested setting.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Fractured multi-turn prompts on the four tested models
reader_labels.reason: The reported decomposed-prompt ASRs are 49.11%–50.89%, so the attack does not make harmful compliance universal or nearly complete (r1–r4).
